solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beanpole to gain upward growth rarely seen before

parts.note: to gain is to win

indicators.note: in a down entry, going upward means the following words are written bottom to top

parts.note: a wart is a small growth on the skin
seld is an archaic word for seldom, a word for rarely used in the past

explanation.surface: A gardener's account of a bean pole that the climbing plant has hardly ever grown up.
explanation.walkthrough: WIN is followed by WART + SELD written upwards, giving WINDLESTRAW, a Scots word for a dry grass stalk and so for a thin, lanky person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a tall, thin, gangling person, the Scots term comparing them to a withered stalk of grass.

clue.text: Local bound to enter my two pubs playing game

indicators.note: to enter means to go into, so the bound sits inside the scrambled letters
playing suggests letters at play, rearranged freely

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: two asks for the pub word to appear twice

parts.note: pub is the singular of the clue's pubs, each one given once
lep is a dialect (local) word for a leap or bound

explanation.surface: A local leaps into my two favourite pubs to play a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like the pub, but it marks a dialect word for a leap. Two copies of the pub word join the letters of my in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old name for a form of whist played without rules, and also a ball game, so it is simply a game.

clue.text: United lead overturning old curse — it's not played down

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for United
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

indicators.note: turning something over flips its order, so the following words are written backwards

parts.note: wo is an old spelling of woe, a curse or misfortune

explanation.surface: A football report: the United captain swearing, in an old-fashioned way, at a match not to be played down.
explanation.walkthrough: An up-bow is a violin stroke drawn from tip to heel, the opposite of a down-bow, hence the cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: String players mark each stroke as up or down, so a stroke that is not a down-stroke is the other kind.

clue.text: Mellow character most often seen in cheese with mould

parts.note: mellow and mild both mean gentle

indicators.note: the letter that turns up most in a given word is the one wanted

parts.note: cheese contains three Es, more than any other letter
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A cheese description: mellow in character, with a bit of mould.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual reading of 'character most often seen' is E as the commonest English letter, but here it is the commonest letter in the word cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildew is a whitish fungal growth, a kind of mould on plants and damp things.

clue.text: Perhaps Jacob's crying, born having to grasp rival's heel

indicators.note: grasping something holds it inside

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for born
having a meal is eating it

indicators.note: a heel is at the back end, so the last letter of a word is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of rival

explanation.surface: The Bible's Jacob crying at birth while grasping his rival brother Esau's heel.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob is not the patriarch but a Jacob sheep, a spotted breed, and its crying is bleating.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jacob is a breed of sheep, and the cry of a sheep is a bleat, so its crying is bleating.

clue.text: Fat idler missing lots of love

indicators.note: something missing has been left out of the word

parts.note: a lollard is an old word for a loller or idler
LOL is the text-message sign-off for lots of love

explanation.surface: A fat layabout who is short of affection.
explanation.walkthrough: LOLLARD loses its opening LOL to leave LARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is rendered pig fat used in cooking.

clue.text: Function packing floor served up mushrooms

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means written from bottom to top
packing something means holding it inside

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
to floor someone is to knock them out, KO

explanation.surface: A catering function where mushrooms were served up from the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Enoki are thin white Japanese mushrooms with tiny caps, grown in clusters.

clue.text: Take ring from love during one rustic dance

parts.note: 'un is a dialect form of one

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits inside it

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
love is nil in tennis, the shape of O

explanation.surface: A love token, a ring, is taken off during a country dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhoop is to remove the hoops, or rings, from something such as a barrel or skirt.

clue.text: Get a beer from regulars in pub if invited

indicators.note: regulars are letters taken at even intervals along the phrase

parts.note: every third letter, starting from the first

explanation.surface: Pub regulars will buy you a beer if you are invited.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'regulars in pub' look like customers, but they are every third letter of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint is the standard serving of draught beer in a British pub.

clue.text: Rheumatoid arthritis returning in weak old beggar

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: pallid means feeble or lacking vigour

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: RA is the medical abbreviation for rheumatoid arthritis

explanation.surface: An old beggar left weak by recurring rheumatoid arthritis.
explanation.definitionFit: Palliard is an archaic term for a vagabond who lived by begging.

clue.text: African group fighting irrational admission?

parts.note: admitting what one is begins I'm
pi is an irrational number

explanation.surface: An African fighting force confessing to acting irrationally.
explanation.walkthrough: The number pi, admitting what it is, would say I'm pi.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a Zulu regiment or band of warriors, a group that fights.

clue.text: Old computer that's crashed I can upgrade finally

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of upgrade

indicators.note: something crashed lies wrecked, its parts in disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone offering to upgrade an old computer that has crashed.
explanation.definitionFit: ENIAC was a 1940s American machine, one of the first electronic general-purpose computers.

clue.text: Mock fool nearly blundering with card, the last trump

indicators.note: blundering means stumbling about clumsily, so the letters are thrown into a new order
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of fool is dropped

explanation.surface: A clumsy jester mocked for fumbling with the trump card in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last trump' looks like card-game talk beside 'card', but it is the definition; 'nearly' trims FOOL to FOO before MOCK, FOO and CARD are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: The crack of doom is the final thunderclap of Judgment Day, heralded by the last trump of the archangel.

clue.text: Grape mould to interfere with German red (only one barrel)

indicators.note: keeping only one of a doubled letter means dropping the other

parts.note: to nobble a horse or juror is to interfere with it
B stands for barrel, one of the two in the word
rot is the German word for red

explanation.surface: Tampering with a German red wine by drawing it from only one barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: NOBBLE has two Bs; keeping only one gives NOBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble rot is the botrytis fungus on grapes, prized because it concentrates sugar for sweet wines.

clue.text: Fix border over piece of decoration

parts.note: to fix a result is to cheat, and do also means cheat

indicators.note: turned over, the word runs backwards

parts.note: a dado is a decorative border along the lower part of a wall

explanation.surface: A decorator's instruction to put up a border above a decorative piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A doodad is an informal word for a small ornament or trinket of no particular use.

clue.text: Talk about having bash in meeting place

indicators.note: having something means holding it within
about suggests letters moved around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a bash is an attempt, a go

explanation.surface: Gossip about a party being held in a meeting place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bash' reads as a party, but it is an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A kgotla is a traditional public assembly, or the place where it meets, in Botswana.

clue.text: Here I am after wandering around Australia — welcome to NZ!

indicators.note: going around something encloses it
wandering about suggests the letters straying out of order

parts.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for Australia

explanation.surface: A traveller arriving in New Zealand after roaming Australia and being greeted.
explanation.definitionFit: Haere mai is the Maori greeting, used across New Zealand to mean welcome or come here.

clue.text: Mining co wanting good supply of temperature resistant alloys

indicators.note: supply here is the adverb from supple, bendily, so the letters are bent into a new order
wanting means lacking, so the letter for good is taken out

explanation.surface: A mining company short of a decent source of heat-proof metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' reads as a noun but is the adverb of supple, the anagram signal. 'wanting good' turns MINING CO into MININCO before it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimonic is a trade name for a family of nickel-chromium alloys used in jet engines because they withstand high heat.

clue.text: Shopper not in for installing TV screen that's movable

indicators.note: installing something puts it inside
not means the named letters are taken away

parts.note: to shop someone is to inform on them
these words removed as written
tele is short for television

explanation.surface: A shopper who has not come in to buy a TV screen that can be moved around.
explanation.walkthrough: A shopper is not a customer but an informer; INFORMANT without IN and FOR leaves MANT, which holds TELE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantelet was a portable shelter or shield wheeled forward to protect besieging soldiers.

clue.text: Minions hampered Gru, a wise criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are twisted into a new order
hampered means held back, so the name is stopped short of its last letter

explanation.surface: In the Despicable Me films, the little yellow Minions get in the way of their boss Gru, a knowing villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minions' looks like the film characters, but it is the definition. 'hampered' cuts GRU to GR, and GR, A and WISE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An earwig, in the old sense, is a flatterer or toady who whispers in a great person's ear, so a minion.

clue.text: Advanced climber on face of K2, vertical in the main

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
the pea is a climbing plant

indicators.note: the face of something is its front, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first character of K2

explanation.surface: An experienced mountaineer on the vertical face of K2.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' and 'K2' conjure a mountaineer, but the climber is a plant. The main is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Apeak is a nautical term for an anchor or oar held upright, and the main is poetic for the sea.

clue.text: Litter lout drops close to bin in hospital

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital

indicators.note: dropping something leaves it out

parts.note: a ned is a young Scottish hooligan

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end

parts.note: the last letter of bin

explanation.surface: A yob drops litter near a bin outside the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' tempts as rubbish, but it is a carried couch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is an enclosed seat carried on poles, a kind of litter.

clue.text: A noodle's trimmed pasta

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: trimmed means cut at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a nellie is a silly person, as is a noodle

explanation.surface: A note that a noodle has been cut into short pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noodle' sounds like pasta already, but it is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Anelli are small ring-shaped pasta, often used in soups.

clue.text: Love to accept a new job with no objection, irrigation worker

indicators.note: the love word accepts, that is takes inside it, the other pieces

parts.note: love is a zero score in tennis

indicators.note: the word job is written without the letters for objection

parts.note: taken as written before removal
OB is a Chambers abbreviation for objection

explanation.surface: Someone takes a job that nobody objects to, as a worker on irrigation.
explanation.walkthrough: A zanjero is a superintendent who manages irrigation canals in the south-western US and Latin America, from Spanish zanja, a ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: The zanjero oversees the distribution of water through ditches and canals, so he is an irrigation official.

clue.text: Embroidery I removed to imitate Mexican blanket

indicators.note: removed means a letter has been taken away

parts.note: zari is South Asian embroidery in gold or silver thread
taken as written
to ape is to imitate

explanation.surface: Copying a Mexican blanket's embroidery while leaving oneself out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A zarape, or serape, is a brightly coloured woollen shawl or blanket worn in Mexico.

clue.text: Awful bile after a lot of Asian breadfruit snack

indicators.note: a lot of but not all means the word loses its end

parts.note: the jak, or jackfruit, is an Asian relative of the breadfruit

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Indigestion brought on by eating too much Asian fruit as a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Jalebi is a South Asian sweet of deep-fried batter spirals soaked in syrup, eaten as a treat.

clue.text: Worthless article ragman's tossed on back of cart

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of cart

indicators.note: tossed about, the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written; the 's is joined to tossed as 'has'

explanation.surface: A rag-and-bone man throwing a useless item onto the back of his cart.
explanation.walkthrough: A ragman is a rag-and-bone man, a street dealer in old clothes and junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Trangam is an archaic word for a trinket or knick-knack of no value.

clue.text: Finds a cranium contains more than one bone

indicators.note: the phrase holds the letters inside it across the word gap

parts.note: the end of Finds, a, and the start of cranium

explanation.surface: An archaeologist's find of a skull containing several bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacra is the plural of sacrum, the triangular bone at the base of the spine.

clue.text: Fantasist to feel remorse returning with gun

parts.note: to gun an engine is to rev it

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word reads right to left

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A daydreamer regretting coming back armed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gun' looks like a weapon but is the verb for revving an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A rêveur is a dreamer, from French, someone lost in fantasy.

clue.text: Armorists love to include inverted heraldic symbols

indicators.note: turned upside down in a down entry, the letters read the other way
the words include the letters within them

parts.note: the last letter of Armorists and the first three of love

explanation.surface: Heraldry experts fond of including upside-down emblems.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a vol is a charge of two wings joined at the base, so vols are such devices.

clue.text: Praise Scottish strike stalling English

indicators.note: stalling something like a horse puts it inside a stall

parts.note: blaud is a Scots verb meaning to strike or slap
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Applauding a Scottish walkout that holds up the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' reads as industrial action, but it is a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: To belaud is to praise lavishly, an intensified form of laud.

clue.text: Cloud burst cutting off street round centre of Wells

indicators.note: going round something surrounds it
cutting off removes the named part

parts.note: taken as written
St is the abbreviation for street

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: the middle letter of Wells

explanation.surface: A cloudburst cuts off a road around the centre of Wells, a cathedral city in Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: To cloud and to blur both mean to make indistinct or hazy.

clue.text: Antics in Stratford shopping arcade needing response

parts.note: a mall is a shopping arcade
an echo is a response

explanation.surface: Some foolery in a Stratford shopping centre that calls for a reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Stratford-upon-Avon is Shakespeare's birthplace, so 'in Stratford' marks a Shakespearean word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's 'miching mallecho' means sneaking mischief, so mallecho is mischievous behaviour.

clue.text: Aussie international's dropped by somebody

indicators.note: something dropped is left out of the word

parts.note: the Wallabies are Australia's national rugby union team
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Australian international player has been dropped by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropped by' reads as a passive, but by is the dropped word.
explanation.definitionFit: Walla, a variant of wallah, means a person connected with something, hence just a person.

clue.text: Pep's life story involving ending in Manchester

indicators.note: involving something takes it inside

parts.note: bio is short for biography, a life story

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of Manchester

explanation.surface: Pep Guardiola's biography covering how his time in Manchester ended.
explanation.walkthrough: Pep looks like Guardiola, the Manchester City manager, but is the definition, meaning vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Pep and brio both mean liveliness and vigour.

clue.text: Passive resistance I contrived with tensive air

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially arranged, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone affecting a tense manner to put up passive resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Vis inertiae is Latin for the force of inertia, a body's tendency to resist being moved, hence passive resistance.
